subject: Discovery recap — MedNext regulated deployment fit & next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Yates <samantha.yates@mednext.health>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + quick context for our regulated inference needs

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for taking time to meet later today. Quick context so the call is focused: MedNext is looking to pilot a clinical summarization feature that will process clinician notes and discharge summaries — these are PHI. Our key constraints: data must remain in our VPC / on-prem environment, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are required, SOC2 evidence and audit logs will be necessary for our security review, and we may need an air-gapped option if the pilot proves sensitive.

Current infra: Kubernetes cluster in our private DC with strict outbound egress rules; EHR integration via HL7/FHIR endpoint. Expected pilot timeline: Q3 (aim to have a working pilot by end of July).

I attached a short outline of our security posture and network topology to this email (mednext-security-outline.pdf).

Would appreciate a discovery call to confirm compatibility and next steps.

Best,
Samantha
Director of Clinical IT
MedNext Health

--
Attachment: mednext-security-outline.pdf (application/pdf, 98 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yates <samantha.yates@mednext.health>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context for our regulated inference needs

Hi Samantha — thanks for the outline and the call earlier. Sending a short recap and next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of pain points (as discussed):
- PHI handling: mednotes must never be persisted outside your controlled environment.
- Key ownership: customer-managed KMS/HSM required for model input/output encryption.
- Network constraints: strict egress, prefer private peering or on-prem runtime; possible air-gap later.
- Compliance evidence: SOC2 artifacts and audit log access required for security review.
- Performance: sub-200ms median token latency for API requests to meet clinician UX targets (pilot scale).

Current stack you shared: on-prem Kubernetes (no public IPs on worker nodes), HL7/FHIR endpoints for ingest, internal VPC + direct connect to AWS for some services.

Success criteria for pilot we captured:
1) Inference requests traverse MedNext network only or a dedicated private link;
2) Keys controlled by MedNext KMS;
3) Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown and audit logs for each request;
4) Deployment packaged for customer security review (SOC2 evidence + architecture diagrams);
5) Pilot sign-off with throughput validated at target latency.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Dev deep technical checklist & port/IP requirements (Dev Patel) — by Tue 2027-05-04.
- You to send detailed network diagram and SOC2 questionnaire responses (Samantha) — by Fri 2027-05-07.
- We’ll provide a Mutual Action Plan and MAP template for procurement and pilot milestones (Ben) — by Wed 2027-05-05.
- Schedule follow-up SE deep dive to map out network routing and KMS integration — proposed Wed 2027-05-10 (I’ll send a calendar invite).

Attachments I’m sending: MVP-deployment-options.pdf (outlines Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private packaging) and MAP-template.xlsx (mutual action plan template). These are starter artifacts — we’ll tailor them once we see your network diagram and SOC2 responses.

If any of the success criteria above are off, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll move to create the MAP and loop in our legal/procurement contacts after we finish the SE deep dive.

Thanks again — excited to see how we can help.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Attachments: MVP-deployment-options.pdf (application/pdf, 220 KB); MAP-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42 KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yates <samantha.yates@mednext.health>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — MedNext regulated deployment fit & next steps

Hi Samantha — quick technical follow-up from our call and Ben’s recap below. I’m trying to capture the checklist I need to validate a Private deployment inside your environment.

On Tue, May 3, 2027 at 5:05 PM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samantha — thanks for the outline and the call earlier. Sending a short recap and next steps so we’re all aligned.

Questions / asks from SE perspective:
- Network topology: can you share the VPC/subnet CIDRs and whether worker nodes have any egress NAT? If you can only share redacted ranges, that’s fine.
- Peering/connectivity: do you have AWS Direct Connect, VPN, or would you prefer an on-prem appliance? Any existing private peering with vendors?
- Egress policy: do outbound connections to our control plane need to be blocked? If so, we can explore a private-control-plane model (control plane in your VPC) or an offline air-gapped installer.
- KMS: which KMS provider do you use (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Thales/HSM)? Will you require HSM-backed keys?
- Audit logs: where should we send logs (syslog/HTTPS endpoint/CloudWatch/etc.) and what retention window do you require?
- Hardware expectations: expected concurrency for pilot (rps) and whether you have NVIDIA A100/RTX series available or would prefer a vGPU/hosted appliance.

Also called out: we have an example ACL/port list for Private deployments and a sample minimal config for an air-gapped install. I’m attaching the sample ACL text file to illustrate which ports we typically need opened for metrics, control plane heartbeats, and model shards sync (example-network-acls.txt).

If you can reply inline to the bullets above or share a small network diagram, that will let us scope the deployment precisely and produce a pilot BOM and timeline.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

--
Attachment: example-network-acls.txt (text/plain, 3 KB)

From: Samantha Yates <samantha.yates@mednext.health>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, procurement@mednext.health
Date: 2027-05-04T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — MedNext regulated deployment fit & next steps

Hi Ben / Dev — thanks for the clear recap and checklist. Quick answers below and attaching the SOC2 questionnaire and a clean network diagram.

- VPC: we’ll share a redacted diagram (attached: mednext-network-diagram.png) and the CIDR ranges in a separate secure doc.
- Connectivity: we have Direct Connect to AWS for certain workloads but prefer an on-prem install for this pilot.
- Egress: general rule is no public egress from worker nodes; outbound to control plane must be explicitly approved.
- KMS: AWS KMS today; we have access to AWS CloudHSM if needed. HSM-backed keys would be preferred for production.
- Logs: send audit logs to our Splunk forwarder over TLS; retention needs to be 3 years for the pilot evidence set.
- Hardware: pilot concurrency estimated 10–20 RPS with burst to 50 for load tests. We have a cluster with spare NVIDIA A40s; if needed we can provision one A100 on an exception basis.
- Procurement: procurement@mednext.health is looped. We expect to work from our standard MSA + SOW; procurement will need the MAP and a ballpark price for a 3-month pilot.
- Timeline: yes — target pilot start late June, validation complete by end of July.

I attached our completed SOC2 questionnaire (mednext_SOC2_questions.pdf) and the network diagram. We’ll also share the detailed CIDR values via the secure folder in the Drive link Ben shared.

Next meeting: Wed 2027-05-10 at 10:00 AM PT works for the SE deep dive. If you can send calendar invite and include an agenda, we’ll confirm.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director of Clinical IT
MedNext Health

--
Attachments: mednext_SOC2_questions.pdf (application/pdf, 430 KB); mednext-network-diagram.png (image/png, 210 KB)
